summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, multiple abdominal surgeries, and recurrent paralytic ileus was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and vomiting over one week. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and electrolyte replacement for hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction but supported a diagnosis of paralytic ileus, with evidence of slow contrast transit. A possible digestive-genital tract fistula was noted, along with mild metabolic acidosis and venous compression, both of which stabilized during the admission. Urine cultures showed no infection. The patient gradually improved, passing flatus and tolerating oral intake, allowing NG tube removal and discharge home. She was advised to continue supplements, avoid opioids, and follow up with gastroenterology and primary care for ongoing management of Crohn’s, fistula, and mental health concerns including depression and PTSD.
